text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Norwegian papers this morning.
-Electricity prices will rise by 15 to 20 percent next year following new tax rules for hydroelectric power plants. However, higher imports of electricity could offset the announced price increase.

-New Finance Minister Jens Stoltenberg says he will continue his predecessor's policy of keeping a tight budget. Stoltenberg says the restrictive economic policy has led to lower unemployment as well as increased welfare.

-Near 50 percent of voters changed party preference between the parlamentary elections in 1993 to the local elections in 1995, a research study shows. The EU election campaign is the main reason for the unstable voting patterns, the study says.

-Shipbuilder and construction group Kvaerner is aiming to be debt-free within two years. Since its takeover of Bristish conglomerate Trafalgar House, Kvaerner has sold assets worth 4.5 billion crowns.

-U.S. investment fund Tiger Management says Resource International Group (RGI) must get Tiger's approval for RGI's merger with Aker. Tiger claims to have a series of private agreements with RGI head Kjell Inge Rkke. Tiger also wants RGI to buy the fund's 62 percent stake in RGI division Norway Seafoods.
